title: The sun compared with other stars
subject: Earth & space

sources.title: NGSS 5-ESS1-1: Support an argument that differences in the apparent brightness of the sun compared to other stars is due to their relative distances from the Earth
OpenStax Astronomy 2e, 1.6 A Tour of the Universe
OpenStax Astronomy 2e, 15 Thinking Ahead (the Sun is a rather ordinary star)
OpenStax Astronomy 2e, 17.1 The Brightness of Stars

note.text: We look out from Earth at the sun by day and the stars by night.
The sun is a star, one of hundreds of billions in our galaxy.
Its light reaches us in about 8 minutes.

steps.title: Another star
steps.instruction: Trace the other star, drawn the same size as the sun.

note.text: The sun is a rather ordinary star: not unusually big or small, hot or cool. Many stars are much like it.
Light from even the nearest other star takes over 4 years to reach us.

steps.title: Near
steps.instruction: Draw the short line from Earth to the sun.

note.text: The sun is close to us, compared with every other star.

steps.title: Far
steps.instruction: Draw the long line from Earth to the other star.

note.text: In real life, this line would be far too long to fit: the nearest other star is about 270,000 times farther than the sun.
note.remember: Other stars are very far away.

steps.title: Argue
steps.question: Why does the sun look so much bigger and brighter than other stars?

options.feedback: Yes. Other stars look faint only because they're so very far away.

options.text: It's the biggest star in the universe
options.feedback: The sun is an ordinary star. Many stars are bigger and brighter: they're just farther away.

options.text: Other stars give off no light
options.feedback: Stars all give off light. They look faint because they're so far away.
They only look tiny. Many are as big as the sun or bigger, but far away.

steps.title: Test the idea
steps.question: Two identical flashlights shine at you. One is near, one is across a field. What do you see?

options.feedback: Right. How bright a light looks depends on how far away it is, as well as how much light it gives off.
They give off the same light, but the far one looks dimmer: distance matters.
Farther lights look dimmer, not brighter.

options.text: You can't see the far one at all
options.feedback: You can see it, just more dimly. That's what happens with distant stars.
